newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Storm kills nine, brings havoc to central Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Storm kills nine, brings havoc to central Vietnam.

text.p: Nine people were killed, hundreds of houses damaged and vast areas of rice paddy submerged by flooding by a tropical storm which hit central Vietnam at the weekend, the Disaster Management Unit (DMU) said on Wednesday.
The DMU, a joint project between the government and the United Nations Development Programme, said in a report that all nine people deaths were in the north-central province of Nghe An.

Some 56,000 households in Nghe An were affected by Typhoon Willie, which weakened to a tropical low pressure system after it landed on Sunday evening. Though it lost momentum, it brought winds of up to 63 miles (101 km) per hour and torrential rains.
The DMU said 70,182 hectares (173,420 acres) of rice fields were still under water in Nghe An and the neighbouring province of Ha Tinh.

Willie was the sixth tropical storm to threaten Vietnam this year. Earlier this month 44 people died and an estimated $300 million worth of damage was caused in seven central provinces, with Ha Tinh the worst hit, when a tropical storm brought heavy rains and flooding.
The latest casualties took to about 440 the number of people who have died in storms and flooding in northern and central regions of the country since the beginning of July.
